artifacts.summary: Five-phase plan unifying the /orchestrate inter-cycle redeploy checkpoint: confirmation + attribution filters so flaky or unrelated findings cannot defer a batch, explicit fast/full depth-disagreement reporting, and finding-naming defer messages.

memory_candidates.content: A verification gate can self-inflict the failure it reports. The /orchestrate inter-cycle redeploy checkpoint ran a full deploy plus the entire shell test suite immediately before taking the findings snapshot it then judged, creating the memory pressure that made a load-sensitive test in that same suite flake -- and deferred an entire task batch over a finding attributable to no task in the batch. The structural lesson: whenever a gate performs heavy work immediately before a measurement, treat any load-sensitive signal in that measurement as unreliable by construction. Two composable filters fix this class without weakening the gate: (1) a confirmation filter -- re-run a candidate blocking finding once and drop it if it does not reproduce, which cannot weaken the gate because a real breakage reproduces; (2) an attribution filter -- drop findings positively shown unrelated to the batch's own modified files. Filter (2) must be fail-safe toward blocking: only findings that POSITIVELY name an identifier absent from the change set are dropped, so a finding naming nothing still blocks. Without that direction the filter degrades into a blanket disable.
